    Wiz uses Claude Code and IDA MCP to find a critical flaw in GitHub

    went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours

    System
    AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling used by Wiz Research: Claude Code (named by The Register and WebProNews) with IDA MCP for automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries (named by Wiz), applied to GitHub.com's backend and GitHub Enterprise Server 3.19.1
    Developer
    Anthropic (Claude Code); the maker of IDA MCP is not named in the sourcesUnited States
    Deployer
    Wiz Research (Sagi Tzadik, Nir Ohfeld, Ronen Shustin, Hillai Ben-Sasson, Yuval Avrahami, Noam Malron)United States
    Jurisdiction
    Not established
    Benefit
    Reported benefit

    Securing GitHub: Wiz Research uncovers Remote Code Execution in GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Server (CVE-2026-3854)

    Independent reporting10 publications
    Date assessed 29 October 2026 Updated 29 October 2026
    Purpose and response for Wiz uses Claude Code and IDA MCP to find a critical flaw in GitHub
    AI system
    AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling used by Wiz Research: Claude Code (named by The Register and WebProNews) with IDA MCP for automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries (named by Wiz), applied to GitHub.com's backend and GitHub Enterprise Server 3.19.1, Not named in the cited sources. Wiz's write-up credits 'AI-augmented tooling, particularly automated reverse engineering using IDA MCP' and does not name Claude. The Register and WebProNews name Claude Code.
    Developer
    Anthropic (Claude Code); the maker of IDA MCP is not named in the sources
    Deployer
    Wiz Research (Sagi Tzadik, Nir Ohfeld, Ronen Shustin, Hillai Ben-Sasson, Yuval Avrahami, Noam Malron)
    Focus
    Cybersecurity
    Purpose
    Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool, built to read a codebase, edit files, run commands and connect to external tools over MCP. Wiz used it, with IDA MCP, to automate reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries. Analyzing code for flaws is within that general purpose. The benefit was an application of what the tool was built to do rather than a departure from it.
    AI contribution
    The AI's documented contribution is speed of analysis, on the researchers' own account. Wiz writes that AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling, particularly IDA MCP, let it rapidly analyze GitHub's compiled binaries and reconstruct internal protocols. Wiz says that speed would not have been feasible manually. Sagi Tzadik told Dark Reading that with AI tools it took under 48 hours from idea to working exploit. The Register adds that the team used Claude Code “to take a lot of the legwork out of the process”. The hypothesis, the exploit, the report and the fix were human work. Six named Wiz researchers confirmed RCE on GHES 3.19.1 and wrote what GitHub called a thorough report. GitHub's security and engineering teams reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed the fix. GitHub's own post, the CVE record and the GHES release notes describe a Bug Bounty report without mentioning AI. The AI-assistance claim therefore rests on Wiz and on outlets quoting Wiz. Wiz's write-up, in the text as read, names IDA MCP and not Claude.

    Spark was built to find bugs and vulnerabilities autonomously by selecting functions to fuzz and generating and running fuzz tests. Finding this flaw was exactly that function, exercised in the vendor's own beta test.
    AI contribution
    On the vendor's account, Spark selected the target, generated the fuzz test and ran it after a single “cifuzz spark” command.     Purpose
    U.S. Customs and Border Protection built the model to identify potentially suspicious patterns in vehicle border-crossing histories, according to the 2024 Artificial Intelligence Roadmap of the Department of Homeland Security. The model flags vehicles for secondary review at ports of entry, and the San Ysidro seizure came from that intended use.
    AI contribution
    The model's contribution was the referral. DHS says it identified a suspicious pattern in the car's border-crossing history and flagged it for review. Mayorkas said the anomaly was identified in 1.4 seconds. The discovery of the narcotics and the arrest were done by officers in secondary review. No source states whether the car would have been referred without the flag. The model's counterfactual contribution is thus asserted by DHS, not demonstrated. The Monitor entry also bundles Mayorkas's claim that AI age-progression imagery has recovered abducted children. That claim names no case, date, or child.

In 2023 an independent comparison by Pierre Goovaerts found that the program's excavation order found lead lines fastest in its first eight months, after which geostatistical rankings would have done better. He concluded that the 2018 decision to stop using the model does not explain this weaker relative result. The field data do not isolate the model's effect on health or spending, and the cost saving came from simulation.

Benefit marks

Depth

The number and color show the depth of a benefit.

  1. 1Depth 1. A convenience, or time or money saved.
  2. 2Depth 2. A measurable improvement in a result or ability.
  3. 3Depth 3. A lasting change, an ability restored, or a risk removed.
  4. 4Depth 4. A serious harm averted or a serious condition resolved in time.
  5. 5Depth 5. A life or livelihood preserved, or a change documented across a population.

Beneficiary

  • Circle: a person
  • Square: an organization
  • Triangle: society

Evidence

  • Solid. A court or regulator found a benefit, or researchers independently studied it.

  • Hatched. Independent reporting.

  • Outline. Claimed by the parties. Only the people or organizations involved, or sources whose independence has not been assessed, support the benefit.

The fill changes with the evidence. The depth color stays the same.
